name: Shree Dharm Mangal Jain Vidyapith Bhojanshala
why_it_matters: Bhojanshala attached to one of the larger Jain dharamshalas at the base of Parasnath Hill (Sammed Shikharji), where 20 of 24 Tirthankaras are believed to have attained moksha. Strict Jain kitchen — pure-veg, no onion, no garlic, no root vegetables. Meals are token-based, served at fixed timings.
insider_tip: Tokens must be bought before each meal slot at the dharamshala office. Lunch around 11:30 am-1 pm, dinner closes well before sunset per Jain rules — plan the parikrama trek to be back in time.
signature_address: Shree Dharm Mangal Jain Vidyapith, Madhuban, Giridih District 825329

name: Shri Rajendra Shanti Vihar Bhojanshala
why_it_matters: Shwetambar Jain dharamshala bhojanshala in Madhuban, the village base for Shikharji parikrama. Token meal prices listed publicly at roughly Rs 30 (breakfast), Rs 50 (lunch), Rs 50 (dinner). Pure Jain kitchen — no onion, no garlic, no root vegetables — and meals end before sunset.
insider_tip: Breakfast (Navkarshi to 9:30 am) is the easiest window for solo trekkers heading up; dinner closes at sunset, so a 6 pm arrival back at Madhuban is the practical cutoff in winter.
signature_address: Shri Rajendra Shanti Vihar, Madhuban, Giridih District 825329
